prompt.title: Listen to your own words
prompt.text: For one day, listen to what you say and think. Catch the phrases that hand your choices to someone else, and rewrite them.
prompt.glossText: The book calls phrases that hand over the choice reactive language, and the alternative proactive.
prompt.whyItMatters: Your words tell you what you believe about who's in charge. Change the words and you start to see the choice again. It's the smallest place to begin, and it works.

form.textPrompt: What did you say or think, word for word?
form.textPlaceholder: e.g. I have to stay late again, they never plan anything.
form.reframePrompt: Say the same thing as a choice you're making.
form.reframePlaceholder: e.g. I'll stay till six tonight, and tomorrow I'll ask for the plan earlier.
form.contextPrompt: Where were you, or who were you talking to?

kindHint.reactive: Words like: I have to, they made me, if only, I can't.
kindHint.proactive: Words like: I choose, I will, I prefer, let's look at options.

checklist.day: Start a listening day and finish it
checklist.phrase: Catch one phrase that gives away the choice

guide.inShort: You'll spend one ordinary day listening to yourself. Each time you hear yourself hand over the choice, you'll note it and rewrite it. A few seconds per phrase. At the end you'll see how your day sounded.
howTo: Tap "Start listening" in the morning. A banner reminds you it's running.
Whenever you catch a phrase, tap "Add phrase" and write it as you said it.
Pick which kind it is. Read the examples under each option if you're unsure.
If it gave away the choice, rewrite it as something you decide.
At the end of the day, tap "End day" and read your summary.
Tap "Mark done" once you've rewritten one phrase. Come back for another day whenever you like.

guide.afterwards: Pick one rewritten phrase and use it out loud this week. Run another listening day in a month and compare the two summaries. Fewer hand-overs is the goal, not zero.
